paragraphs.sourceText: With the rapid progress in the economy, it is natural that people’s ideology is bound for change. Being 26 is no longer a virtue to some people, and they are not alone in holding this view. Each might have different viewpoints on how to lead one’s lifestyle: some prefer simplicity, some love luxuries, some spend 27 , some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse. As I was born poor and in the countryside, the simple rural life seldom loses its 28 to me, but as my station changes, I have an opportunity to 29 with the newly rich, an experience which has revolutionized my view of lifestyle.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着经济的快速进步，人们的思想观念自然也必然发生变化。对于一些人来说，节俭不再是一种美德，而且持这种观点的人也不止他们一个。每个人对于如何过上自己的生活方式可能有不同的看法：有些人喜欢简单，有些人喜欢奢侈，有些人挥霍无度，有些人像乡下老鼠一样积累。由于我出身贫寒，生活在农村，简单的乡村生活对我来说很少失去吸引力，但随着身份的转变，我有机会与新富打交道，这种经历彻底改变了我的生活方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is evil or sinful to spend little and to save much, an idea only recently being revealed to me. Actually the whole world is in a 30 to borrow and to spend, with the USA leading the trend. The USA is still the richest and most powerful country in the world, but the 31 is that they borrow money from us. Though a 32 of economics, at least I know that investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into the 33 rather than the decent and kind lender. An apparent case is real estate. Those who are 34 and have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. Even education is not immune from this theory. Many of those poor parents who have the vision to send their children to college have benefited from this investment, even though they have to 35 a living. It is reasonable to conclude that spending is praiseworthy, supposing it is not beyond your means.
paragraphs.translationZh: 少花多存是邪恶的或有罪的，这是最近才向我透露的一个想法。事实上，全世界都在疯狂借贷和消费，其中美国引领了潮流。美国仍然是世界上最富有、最强大的国家，但讽刺的是他们向我们借钱。虽然我是个经济学门外汉，但至少我知道用借来的钱进行投资会把借款人变成掠夺者，而不是正派和善良的贷款人。一个明显的例子是房地产。那些精明的、从银行贷款的人，通过以高出几倍的价格出售所购买的房屋，变得相对富裕。甚至教育也不能幸免于这一理论。许多有志送孩子上大学的贫困父母都从这项投资中受益，尽管他们必须勉强维持生计。有理由得出这样的结论：花钱是值得赞扬的，前提是它不超出你的能力范围。

paragraphs.sourceText: Are Forgotten Crops the Future of Food?
paragraphs.translationZh: 被遗忘的农作物是食物的未来吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles (腌菜) and salads. “It’s not very well-known,” says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan (龙眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. “We have to grow what is profitable,” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 在马六甲海峡附近的一个小果园里，林国安 (Lim Kok Ann) 只种了一棵树，一种脆脆的酸浆果，马来西亚人主要用在泡菜和沙拉中。 “它不是很出名，”这位 45 岁的人说，他把重点放在龙眼浆果和菠萝上，因为它们有更大的市场。 “我们必须发展有利可图的业务，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. They’re pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called “alternative” crops — such as kedondong. At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. “Anything you see here is a forgotten crop,” says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia’s capital Kuala Lumpur.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但在距离马来西亚乡村不到一小时的地方，在三个巨大的银色圆顶内，科学家们正在试图改变食物的未来。他们通过种植和加工所谓的“替代”作物（例如 kedondong）来突破人类饮食的界限。在全球研究中心“未来作物” (CFF) 的总部，这种未充分利用的特殊水果已被制成无糖果汁，富含维生素 C，并在感官评估中获得最高分。 “你在这里看到的任何东西都是被遗忘的作物，”赛义德·阿扎姆-阿里 (Sayed Azam-Ali) 谈到马来西亚首都吉隆坡郊外 CFF 花园中茂密的植物时说道。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops — wheat, maize, rice and soybean — provide two-thirds of the world’s food supply. “We’re dependent on these four,” he says. “But actually there’re 7,000 crops we’ve been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those.” Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops — plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or “alternative” as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 阿扎姆-阿里教授解释说，仅四种作物——小麦、玉米、大米和大豆——就提供了世界三分之二的粮食供应。 “我们依赖这四个，”他说。 “但实际上，我们已经种植了 7,000 种农作物数千年。我们忽略了所有这些。”研究人员正试图释放这些被忽视的作物的潜力——他们将这些植物描述为被遗忘、未被充分利用或“替代”的植物，因为它们被主要作物加工成分驱动的日益统一的饮食所取代。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) It’s a timely quest. The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 这是一个及时的任务。食品行业已占全球温室气体排放量的近三分之一。据估计，到 2050 年，世界粮食产量必须增加 50%，才能养活预计的全球 100 亿人口。在不加剧气候变化的情况下满足这一需求需要紧急解决方案。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Forgotten crops hold key answers. By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient (具有气候韧性的) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. His summary is plain: “Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 被遗忘的农作物蕴藏着关键答案。通过投资被忽视的当地植物，各国可以减少对进口作物及其高碳供应链的依赖。在气候变暖威胁现有农作物之际，恢复人类曾经食用的农作物品种也可以提高粮食安全。阿扎姆-阿里认为，最重要的是，被遗忘的作物是最能适应气候变化且营养丰富的作物之一。他的总结很简单：“饮食多样化对人类的未来至关重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Food security experts agree. “There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance,” says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. “Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are,” she adds.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 食品安全专家同意。新加坡国立大学水政策研究所高级研究员塞西莉亚·托尔塔贾达（Cecilia Tortajada）表示：“世界上并不存在粮食不安全，而是对粮食的无知。” “每当我们拥有本土作物时，我们往往会忽视它们，就好像它们没有价值一样，但它们确实有价值，”她补充道。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Azam-Ali knows that scepticism firsthand. He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. But “the resistance was enormous,” he recalls.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 阿扎姆-阿里亲身体验过这种怀疑。 20 世纪 80 年代，他通过在尼日尔遇到的女农民的工作发现了替代作物。这位当时的博士生记得，他对自己在后院种植的农作物感到惊叹，在没有技术的帮助下，当大作物歉收时，他们只能养家糊口。他看到了建立替代食品系统的巨大机会。但“阻力是巨大的，”他回忆道。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Undeterred, he ploughed on. Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. “That’s the critical thing,” he says. In one of the centre’s domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa (辣木粉) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten (谷胶) and higher in nutrients. Tan’s job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. “I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes.” says Tan, who is also a trained chef. It’s a strategy to appeal to the world’s growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. It’s also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as “old or poor people’s food” or as inferior “women’s crops”, adds Tan.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 他没有被吓倒，继续努力。一个又一个的项目帮助证明这些作物作为主要作物的替代品在不同的环境中都是可行的。但这些作物是否有销路的问题仍然存在。 “这是关键的事情，”他说。在该中心的一个圆顶内，食品技术员谭新林用辣木粉粉代替一些小麦粉，烘烤出谷胶含量较低、营养成分较高的蛋糕。谭的工作是用这些仍然不熟悉的原料创造食谱，以吸引当地和国际口味。近年来，她使用了 CFF 种植的一些被遗忘的作物，例如辣木和班巴拉花生，来制作从即食汤到印度小吃的各种食品。 “我尝试对被遗忘的作物进行现代化改造，而不是使用旧的食谱。”谭说，他也是一名训练有素的厨师。这一战略旨在吸引世界上不断壮大的中产阶级，他们越来越多地转向快餐和加工食品行业。谭补充道，这也是一种帮助扭转人们对当地农作物“老人或穷人的食物”或劣质“女性农作物”的看法。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. “African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it,” says Azam-Ali. “Colonial powers said you can’t grow that because there’s no oil. We can’t get a market for it.” But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF’s best reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 当地食物的这些内涵的根源可以很深。班巴拉花生是撒哈拉以南非洲地区富含蛋白质的本土作物，东南亚部分地区也有种植，其边缘化可以追溯到殖民统治。 “种植班巴拉花生的非洲妇女实际上因种植而受到惩罚，”阿扎姆-阿里说。 “殖民国家说你不能种植它，因为没有石油。我们找不到它的市场。”但如今，班巴拉穆鲁库 (bambara murukku) 已成为 CFF 评价最好的食品之一，他们的目标是将其引入杂货店，向潜在投资者展示藜麦等农作物的成功。大约 30 年前，藜麦在玻利维亚和秘鲁的原生山区之外几乎闻所未闻。如今，这种营养丰富的谷物出现在世界各地豪华餐厅的菜单上。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. Ever since the “green revolution” of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. Today “nutrition is becoming a time bomb”, says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 通过营养而不是产量来衡量作物是被遗忘的食品企业的核心。自20世纪60年代“绿色革命”以来，高产作物一直主导着现代农业。在世界需要增加粮食供应之际，这在一定程度上是对毁灭性饥荒的关键反应。如今，“营养正在成为一颗定时炸弹”，阿扎姆-阿里说，因为不断增加的二氧化碳水平剥夺了农作物的矿物质。他断言，我们不应该对主要农作物进行生物强化，而应该投资于那些被遗忘的、本来就更有营养的农作物。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) In the bowels of CFF’s third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre’s “crown jewels”, revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. It’s one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. This research is “the game changer”, says Azam-Ali, ensuring that “future crops” are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 在 CFF 的第三个圆顶内部，实验室经理 Gomathy Sethuraman 打开一扇窗户，通向中心的“皇冠上的宝石”，露出在明亮的黄色灯光下生长的四棱豆藤蔓。这是科学家们研究高温和二氧化碳水平对替代作物营养构成影响的多个房间之一。阿扎姆-阿里表示，这项研究“改变了游戏规则”，确保“未来作物”在温暖气候下也是最健康的。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world’s first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 美国智囊团 Food Tank 总裁丹妮尔·尼伦伯格 (Danielle Nierenberg) 表示，全球范围内围绕被遗忘食物的势头正在不断增强。除了自称为世界上第一个专门研究未充分利用作物的研究中心的 CFF 之外，还有其他倡导农业多样性的重要团体，包括作物信托、慢食、Icrisat 和国际生物多样性组织。她说，更多的中等收入消费者正在寻找营养食品，而其他人则渴望尝试祖父母曾经吃过的未加工食品。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 但是，在某些地区，人们对被遗忘的食物的兴趣日益浓厚，但在另一些地区，高糖、高脂肪和加工食品的西式饮食在全球范围内的传播却超过了这种兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is “the obsession with imported products”, says Jenifer Kuah, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country’s small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a “status symbol”, she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 例如，在马来西亚促进当地农作物衰退的一个主要障碍是“对进口产品的痴迷”，吉隆坡富裕郊区一家倡导本地食品的餐厅的联合创始人 Jenifer Kuah 说。她说，锡特卡被视为该国小型农场到餐桌餐饮领域的先驱，但顾客仍然寻求外国食材作为“地位的象征”。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. “Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change,” says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City, University of London. We “have to get used to eating other crops” as yields of staple crops fall, he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: O）关于被遗忘的食物的争论感觉很直观。一些分析人士表示，这实际上是不可避免的。伦敦城市大学食品政策教授蒂姆·朗表示：“气候变化几乎肯定意味着人们的口味将被迫改变。”他说，随着主要农作物产量下降，我们“必须习惯吃其他农作物”。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. According to a senior researcher, we will have secure food supply if we rid ourselves of ignorance about native crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 据一位高级研究员称，如果我们摆脱对本土作物的无知，我们将拥有安全的粮食供应。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Most of the world’s food supply comes from a tiny number out of thousands of crops that have been grown for centuries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 世界上大部分粮食供应来自种植了几个世纪的数千种农作物中的极少数。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. To provide their family with food when the staple crops failed, some African women farmers grew local crops in their backyards.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 为了在主粮作物歉收时为家人提供食物，一些非洲女农民在自家后院种植当地作物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. High-yielding crops have occupied a dominant position in modern agriculture since the green revolution in the last century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39、上世纪绿色革命以来，高产作物在现代农业中占据主导地位。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Growing alternative crops proved feasible in a variety of environments, but the critical question was whether they would be marketable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 事实证明，种植替代作物在各种环境下都是可行的，但关键问题是它们是否有销路。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. According to a professor, when the yields of staple crops fall, we will have to adapt to eating foods from alternative crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 根据一位教授的说法，当主要作物的产量下降时，我们将不得不适应吃替代作物的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Urgent measures have to be taken to provide food for the projected world population without aggravating the climate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 必须采取紧急措施，在不加剧气候的情况下为预计的世界人口提供粮食。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Colonial rule marginalised local crops by punishing Africans who grew them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 殖民统治通过惩罚种植当地作物的非洲人，使当地作物边缘化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. As existing crops are endangered by global warming, we can increase food security by bringing back the many forgotten food crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 由于现有作物受到全球变暖的威胁，我们可以通过恢复许多被遗忘的粮食作物来加强粮食安全。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Researchers are trying to find out how higher temperatures and CO₂ levels affect the nutritional composition of alternative crops.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 研究人员正在试图找出更高的温度和二氧化碳水平如何影响替代作物的营养成分。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Imagine you’re an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. You stumble into a movie theatre that’s showing the latest Hollywood horror film.
paragraphs.translationZh: 想象一下，您是一名外星人，被派到地球来记录居住在地球上的哺乳动物的行为。您无意中走进一家正在放映最新好莱坞恐怖电影的电影院。

paragraphs.sourceText: Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. They’re all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 几十个人聚集在一间漆黑、未装修的房间里。他们都盯着一个矩形区域，上面的光线图案快速变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们显然处于高度兴奋的状态。他们的心率加快，时而紧张地环顾四周，时而在座位上集体跳跃，并发出高亢的警告声。

paragraphs.sourceText: Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最终，灯光亮起，矩形屏幕变黑。人类有说有笑地起身离开房间，脸上流露出喜悦的表情。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么这些人自愿让自己经历看似非常不愉快的经历？为什么它们对屏幕上的光图案反应如此强烈？

paragraphs.sourceText: I am fascinated with the paradox of horror — the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我对恐怖的悖论着迷——许多人寻求恐怖娱乐的奇怪事实。

paragraphs.sourceText: I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我认为这个难题的答案在于人性。

paragraphs.sourceText: My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. You can see these elements of horror in children’s games. Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我的研究表明，我们人类进化到能够在安全的环境中体验负面情绪的情况下寻找快乐。你可以在儿童游戏中看到这些恐怖元素。以捉迷藏为例，这是对捕食者与猎物相互作用的模拟。孩子躲起来，大人假装成掠食者，一边寻找孩子，一边像危险的野兽一样嚎叫。

paragraphs.sourceText: This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种模拟为孩子们提供了如何避免成为猎物的重要信息，孩子们往往会发现这种活动非常令人满意，大概是因为它让他们在潜在的灾难性场景中获得了安全的体验。

paragraphs.sourceText: They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution’s way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们觉得这是令人愉快的，而愉悦是进化激励我们采取适应性行为的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.
paragraphs.translationZh: 恐怖对许多人来说是令人愉悦的，因为它让我们能够应对负面情绪并制定应对策略。我们了解真正害怕的感觉，并学习如何处理负面情绪。

paragraphs.sourceText: How, then, does horror work? My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms — an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，恐怖是如何发挥作用的呢？我的研究表明，恐怖是通过利用一套古老的生物防御机制——一种进化的恐惧系统，我们与其他动物共有的——来发挥作用的。但人类具有独特的想象力，我们利用进化后的想象力进入充满危险的虚拟世界。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you’re not a loyal horror fan. If you make it through the film in one piece, you’ll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?
paragraphs.translationZh: 即使您不是忠实的恐怖片粉丝，观看恐怖片也是有充分理由的。如果你完整地看完了这部电影，你可能会体验到一种强烈的掌控感，一种你能够度过一段可怕经历的感觉。不管怎样，看恐怖片可以让你更好地处理自己的恐惧，谁知道什么时候这会变得至关重要呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现实世界正在发生一场觉醒，反对多年来强加给我们的美丽模式。但在数字领域，社交媒体决定了什么被认为是美丽的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don’t correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become “legitimate”. At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
paragraphs.translationZh: 两种对立的斗争正在同时进行。在物质世界中，这场斗争与女性承受的潜在压力背道而驰，她们要遵守不切实际的美丽理想。作为斗争的一部分，各种媒体都报道了身体不符合所谓理想的女性。所有那些以前被排除在杂志、电视剧封面和公共议程之外的女性，现在都变得“合法”了。与此同时，一群有影响力的人开始在社交媒体上上传自己未化妆的照片，甚至是强调所谓缺陷的照片。

paragraphs.sourceText: Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the “cyborg look”, which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科技重塑了我们的美丽理想，并在向大众传达这一信息方面做得非常出色。过去十年的奇异遗产之一是“赛博格造型”的流行，它描绘了 2050 年美国人的样子。

paragraphs.sourceText: The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 半机械人的造型迅速传播开来。然而如今，Instagram 面孔已成为新的美丽理想。

paragraphs.sourceText: The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified (游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms — the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当积极参与学习过程时，公认的美丽规范的内化会更加有效。用户的积极参与体现在社交媒体平台提供的游戏化互动中——点赞、发表评论、比较、分享的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一旦所需的美丽理想被内化，用户就会获得工具或功能来改变自己的外观以适应公认的美丽理想，例如编辑图像、选择理想的滤镜、正确的背景。

paragraphs.sourceText: A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在美国进行的一项调查显示，超过 50% 的人在发布图片之前会对其进行过滤。听说其中大多数是女性，您不会感到惊讶。强迫性过滤的一个重要后果是，人们开始倾向于将自己视为一个需要观察和评价的对象，就像另一个人从侧面观察和判断一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and Face Tune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.
paragraphs.translationZh: 滤镜的效果已经远远超出了友善的娱乐。过滤器和网络上玩的整个游戏都会影响用户的心理健康。一项研究表明，Instagram、Snapchat 和 Face Tune 等应用程序可以让用户达到以前只能在美容杂志中观察到的完美水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管人类一向珍视美丽，但在过去的十年里，我们对外表的痴迷达到了前所未有的顶峰。人们花在社交媒体上的时间产生了一种想要实现不可能的美丽理想的冲动，这种冲动如此强烈，以至于唯一能解决这个问题的不是美容干预，而是心理健康护理。
